In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate". He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsula it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use. "There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said. The Ukrainian president pointed to images online of tanks and other Russian military hardware using the route from Russia into occupied Crimea as a supply line and for logistics. The Ukrainian president added that Russia had carried out attacks with missiles and drones on bridges in Ukraine. items.headline: Displaced Palestinians protest as Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza
items.blurb: Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings as part of a 'gradual displacement' policy, a Gaza mayor says.
items.text: Hundreds of displaced Palestinians have protested as Israeli forces continue to destroy residential buildings in Gaza, beyond the line they withdrew to under last year’s ceasefire. Al Jazeera journalist Moath al-Kahlout, reporting from Gaza’s Deir el-Balah, said displaced Palestinians who live in the area near the “Yellow Line” gathered on Saturday to demonstrate against Israel’s intensifying air strikes. The “ Yellow Line” separates Israeli- and Hamas-controlled areas in Gaza since the “ceasefire” signed in October 2025. “More than 500 housing units have been destroyed in less than a month,” said Mohammed Musleh, mayor of Deir-el Balah’s Maghazi municipality, told Al Jazeera. “This is part of what appears to be a systematic policy of gradual creeping displacement aimed at forcing residents out of their camp and destroying as many homes as possible,” Musleh said. Gaza’s Ministry of Public Works and Housing says 350,000 families are homeless after Israeli attacks destroyed 80 percent of the enclave’s homes. items.text: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10–18ft are expected, with local sets of 18–22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. items.blurb: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone attack on the vessel.
items.text: A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say. The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment. "War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor." Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies. The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments. The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex. items.blurb: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
items.text: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa , on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions. The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer. The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago , when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park , owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. items.headline: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
items.blurb: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.
items.text: Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock and have been suspended for the night, after running more than a day over time, as countries have been unable to agree on a new global climate deal. The EU and Pacific island nations are amongst a group pushing back against the latest draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels. A second sticking point involves a push from the Africa Group to get commitments on more money for adaptation - but the EU has previously said it would not support this. Negotiating teams due to fly out on Sunday morning are now moving their flights to Monday in a sign that a deal is not yet in sight. If countries cannot reach consensus - which is required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended. In that case the summit would end with no deal and be reconvened next year. This has only happened once before since countries started holding COP climate meetings in 1995. On Saturday,

items.text: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday. Younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). items.text: A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities. Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said. Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added. Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition. Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House. Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile. items.blurb: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has invoked rarely used provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act to investigate the six Indian citizens arrested across India for allegedly facilitating drug transactions in the United States, people aware of the investigation said.
items.text: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has invoked rarely used provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act to investigate the six Indian citizens arrested across India for allegedly facilitating drug transactions in the United States, people aware of the investigation said. Sections 12 and 24 of the act empower the federal agency to act against individuals in India who engage in or control drug trade involving substances sourced and supplied on foreign soil. Section 12 of the NDPS act prohibits external dealings in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances without prior authorisation from the central government. It specifically bars any person from engaging in or controlling trade in which such substances are obtained outside India and supplied to another person outside India, unless authorised by the government. Section 24 prescribes rigorous imprisonment of 10 to 20 years, along with a fine of ₹ 1 lakh to ₹ 2 lakh, for violating this provision. The decision was taken unanimously by all 25 directors due to the drought situation and the difficulties faced by farmers, Patil, a former MLA, said. The union has also decided to raise the procurement rates paid to milk producers by ₹3 per litre for buffalo milk and ₹2 per litre for cow milk, he said, adding that this hike was "historic". "The revised rates will come into effect from November 21 and remain applicable for around 131 days, till March. The situation will be reviewed every month, and the board will take further decisions depending on the circumstances," Patil said. He said milk availability was likely to decline significantly across Maharashtra, including Kolhapur district, and the union would have to take decisions accordingly. items.blurb: California AG Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang violated state laws by misleading investors over alleged chip sales to China. The probe could lead to civil penalties or criminal proceedings against the chipmaker.
items.text: Trouble continues to mount for chipmaking company Nvidia after its former CEO, Jensen Huang, was caught up in a string of controversies and eventually had to step down on November 12. According to Bloomberg , California, which has already begun a probe into whether Nvidia illegally sold advanced chips to China despite US restrictions and misled investors about its conduct, is also looking into potential criminal violations of state law. Raising the stakes for the chipmaker, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Friday (local time) that the company or Huang may have violated several state laws if they shared false information with the public regarding such sales. Bonta announced the investigation on Thursday, and it is still at a preliminary stage. The report added that the probe has not reached any conclusions yet. Those pressures combined to weigh on US markets through Friday, with all key US indexes closing sharply down on the day, furthering earlier falls over the week. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average were pushed into correction territory, a point where they are trading at 10% or more down from a recent high. items.text: Amazon is nearing a $7.5 billion deal to acquire AI startup Decart, as the tech giant looks to improve chip efficiency and strengthen Amazon Web Services' (AWS) competition with Nvidia, according to the Financial Times. The talks are at an advanced stage, and a deal could be finalised as soon as early next week, the FT reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Decart's software allows AI models to run more efficiently, freeing up computer chip capacity. An acquisition could help AWS compete with Nvidia, whose graphics processing units (GPUs) are widely used to power AI workloads. Amazon launched its Trainium3 AI chip in late 2025 to rival Nvidia. Decart was an early adopter of Trainium3 and uses the chips to power its products. The startup had also held talks with Nvidia, Crypto Briefing reported. Founded in 2023 by three Israeli engineers, Decart was valued at $4 billion in May after raising $300 million from investors including Radical Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Benchmark and Nvidia. Companies such as Rooter are looking to capitalise on this growing market by bringing gamers, content creators and publishers onto a single platform. Rising mobile gaming adoption and new monetisation avenues have further increased interest in the segment. Founded in 2016 by Piyush Kumar and Dipesh Agarwal, Rooter operates a gaming live-streaming and commerce platform that allows users to stream and watch gameplay across popular titles such as BGMI, Call of Duty and Valorant, while engaging with gaming creators. The company has also entered gaming commerce, selling in-game currencies and gift cards to build a revenue stream beyond advertising and content. Rooter’s strategy appears to be gaining traction, with the company more than doubling its operating revenue to Rs 170.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 78.9 crore in the previous financial year, while narrowing its losses by 40% to Rs 19.2 crore, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr . items.headline: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
items.blurb: Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps.
items.text: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI. Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” “Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.” Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS. items.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.blurb: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. items.headline: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
items.blurb: Test using prompts with unique, trackable secrets proves that data doesn't stay private.
items.text: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. items.text: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.” “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.” In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating

These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. items.headline: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing?
items.blurb: Lenders don't want SpaceX shooting their collateral into orbit. What does that mean for space data centers writ large?
items.text: The push to build data centers in space faces plenty of obstacles, from tricky engineering to a dearth of rockets that could take chips to orbit. But what about paying for the chips? The data center ecosystem currently depends on debt financing, with cloud providers borrowing to build out data centers and then paying back the loans with a share of the revenue. Those deals typically use the chips as collateral — if the data centers default on their loans, the lenders can take possession of the chips and resell them. That backstop makes it cheaper for companies to finance their chips. Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research , some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024. But you’re not going to repossess chips installed in a satellite orbiting 300 miles above Earth at 17,500 miles per hour. Over the past year, the company has churned out a gush of popular live-action romances like “Crossing the Line with My Neighbor,” “Accidentally Married My Boss,” and “Spoiled by My Billionaire Sugar Daddy.” Lately, however, the company’s homepage is covered in AI-generated content. The reason isn’t exactly hard to figure out: the production overhead for AI content is substantially less than live-action. The profit potential, meanwhile, is substantially higher, if you can draw an audience. Its latest microdrama premiered in Los Angeles last week. items.text: One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called “killer robots.” Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to “start discussing options” after a largely fruitless week of negotiations. Before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, said it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo. The compromise reached was that countries would instead have two years to propose regulations. Negotiations between countries on which regulations to adopt and how to enforce them will likely drag on well beyond that. Additionally, room was left for some of those yet-to-be-adopted regulations to remain “optional.” Humanitarian organizations and some countries see a need to urgently adopt legally binding rules as semi-autonomous weapons and drones have been responsible for a significant number of civilian deaths in conflicts around the globe, including in Ukraine , Gaza , and Sudan. items.blurb: Lawsuit: Over 99% of school system’s AI gun alerts were false positives.
items.text: In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed. The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t. According to a lawsuit filed by the current and former students, Taki Allen, Yui-Osa Ogbeide, Devon Thompson Jr., and Keith Winfield III, due to “both technological and human errors,” school officials called police to the scene anyway, and the cops responded with force. items.text: Sarvam AI's Token Factory launch has brought India's emerging inference-as-a-service market into focus, with L&T, E2E Networks' Jarvislabs, Utho Labs and Mirror Security also building offerings around token-based AI infrastructure. Token factories allow developers and enterprises to access multiple AI models through APIs and pay for the tokens they consume, without having to manage GPU infrastructure or model deployment themselves. As AI adoption drives demand for inference, Indian infrastructure players are looking to move beyond GPU rentals and monetise computing capacity through managed services, with an opportunity to serve both domestic and global workloads. Sarvam AI’s latest announcement of its Token Factory has brought a new layer of India’s artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure ecosystem into focus. The Bengaluru-based startup on November 16 launched a commercial platform that allows developers and enterprises to access multiple AI models through its computing infrastructure. items.headline: Scaler Cofounder Anshuman Singh Unveils AI Training Data Venture Arcfront
items.blurb: Tech upskilling platform Scaler’s cofounder Anshuman Singh has unveiled Arcfront, an AI research and training data venture that turns records…
items.text: Scaler cofounder Anshuman Singh has unveiled Arcfront with Naman Bhalla, claiming four of the five frontier AI labs became customers within a year. Arcfront is commercialising records of expert decision-making to help AI developers train and test models on professional tasks that require judgement beyond producing correct answers. Arcfront operates under Evaratus Inc., with company recruitment material identifying Evaratus as formerly Scaler AI Labs. Its current ownership relationship with Scaler remains unconfirmed. Tech upskilling platform Scaler’s cofounder Anshuman Singh has unveiled Arcfront, an AI research and training data venture that turns records of how professionals solve problems into material for training and testing advanced AI models. Singh is building the venture with Naman Bhalla, Scaler’s former head of AI products and an ex-Google software engineer. In a post on X, Singh said Arcfront also has “deep support” from Scaler cofounder Abhimanyu Saxena. Singh claimed that four of the five frontier AI labs became Arcfront’s customers within less than a year of operations. However, he did not identify the labs. Arcfront operates under Evaratus Inc., according to its website’s legal disclosures.
